newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks follow Dow surge at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks follow Dow surge at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened modestly firmer on Thursday, the market responding in a lukewarm fashion to a wave of buying on Wall Street after the U.S. election which saw the Republican party keep control of Congress.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 9.1 points at 2,369.7.
The December share price index was seven points firmer at 2,382 and at a 12.3 point premium to the underlying index.
As in the past few sessions, volume was thin with only the main blue chip industrial and resource issues finding any trading interest early.
"The bullish sentiment for this market has run its course over the last few weeks and now there is no supportive interest," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney brokerage Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said that with the Dow stronger and interest rates lowered, most factors were positive for the market but investors were still waiting to see stronger earnings from Australian companies.

Key resource issues CRA and WMC opened lower despite stronger base metal prices on the London Metal Exchange on Wednesday. Industrial issues fared better, with the retail and insurance sectors finding buying support.
